symphony_capabilities.reason: Current official Symphony uses app-server thread/start plus turn/start; its dynamic tool schema has no async field. Retries create fresh threads.

ineligible.linear_graphql: Mixed read/write tool without a durable async call/result/cancel contract
ineligible.hosted_tools: OpenAI async calling supports client function/custom tools only
ineligible.programmatic_tools: Async must not be combined with programmatic tool calling

execution: Act with initiative inside the stated authority and continue until the acceptance evidence is complete or a concrete gate blocks progress.
Resolve instruction conflicts by priority and recency; preserve explicit safety and authority boundaries, and state any unresolved conflict.
Use concise, direct prose. Lead progress and final reports with outcomes and evidence.
Use Astra only when all task capabilities are proven and a cheaper eligible model is inadequate; honor the supplied attempt, token, cost, and wall-time budget.
delegation: Delegate only bounded, independent work when policy and capacity permit; keep one owner per mutable surface and integrate only verified results.
Do not create a competing controller, queue, wait/message layer, or steering protocol.
testing: Calibrate tests to changed risk: exercise failure modes, state transitions, integrations, and the repository's exact CI selector.
Keep source, local tests, hosted CI, deployment, runtime, and dogfood evidence as separate proof tiers.
state: Use Responses API for Astra tool calling and preserve prior response/reasoning state when the transport supports it.
Keep stable prompt prefixes cacheable; use configuration updates only where supported and never adjacent or with incompatible compaction modes.
Treat accepted steering as connection-local queued input: it does not undo output or cancel an already-started tool. Reconcile by native IDs and receipts after disconnect.
